name: Korgalzhyn State Nature Reserve (Tengiz-Korgalzhyn Lakes)
blurb: Saline lakes and steppe: northern flamingos, pelicans, saiga and wolves.

tip.title: Remove the saiga
tip.text: Saiga graze the steppe and feed wolves and foxes. Set Saiga antelope to -100% and watch wolves, then foxes turn harder on marmots and wetland birds.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Saryarka - Steppe and Lakes of Northern Kazakhstan

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Powers the steppe grasses, reeds and the algae of the shallow, sunlit lakes.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead grass, reeds, algae and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil and lake water.

nodes.name: Feather grasses
nodes.desc: Tussock grasses typical of the Kazakh steppe, grazed by saiga and marmots.
Reedbeds line the freshwater parts of the wetlands, and pelicans nest on islands or in dense aquatic vegetation such as reeds.

nodes.name: Microalgae and diatoms
nodes.desc: Blue-green algae and diatoms in the lake water feed brine shrimp, midge larvae and flamingos.
Small crustaceans of salt lakes that filter algae; flamingos filter-feed on brine shrimp.
Larvae of non-biting midges live in lake mud and are eaten by flamingos and many waterbirds.
Dabbling duck of the shallows, eating seeds and aquatic invertebrates; huge numbers of ducks use the lakes on migration.
Filters crustaceans, midge larvae and algae from shallow lakes. Korgalzhyn holds the northernmost breeding population.
Fish-eating wetland bird nesting on islands or in reeds; the reserve is said to hold about a tenth of the world population.
Large water frog of the lake margins that eats insects and is itself eaten by foxes and harriers.
Opportunist that preys on marmots, birds and frogs, takes saiga young and raids pelican nests when water levels fall.

nodes.name: Grey wolf
nodes.desc: The steppe predator of the reserve and the main threat to adult saiga; it also hunts marmots.
Raptor of reedbeds that hunts waterbirds, frogs and flamingo chicks across the wetlands.
